summary: Build an n8n workflow that starts when a taxpayer uploads W-2 and 1099 images, sorts each document by type, extracts the figures with a Claude model, and assembles a draft 1040-SR with source references for each number. A stronger, different Claude model checks the draft against a fixed checklist, and a trained Kushim employee approves every return before anything is released.

tools.role: Runs the workflow on each intake upload: routes documents by type, calls the Claude steps, applies the fixed tax-form steps and the spouse-death pause rule, and holds each draft for employee approval.
Connects the workflow to the intake upload and the draft store, with no AI involved.
Sets the standing brief for each Claude step: work only from the uploaded documents, mark every figure with its source, and never guess a missing value.
Holds the current-year Form 1040-SR instructions, the checklist used by the checker, and the house rules, so the AI relies on these rather than memory.
Tests the extraction and checker steps on sample returns, including incomplete and conflicting documents, before any change goes live.
Traces each run with a metadata-only allowlist, so failures can be investigated without sensitive tax content reaching the telemetry service.

shortlist.reason: A visual workflow triggered by uploads fits an intake that receives documents all day, and the steps, approval gates and pause rules stay visible to the reviewer. It also suits an IT team that can maintain it.
shortlist.tradeoff: Its licence allows only internal business use, so the firm must not resell it, and someone must build and maintain the workflow.

shortlist.reason: The Claude app with a saved skill can produce a draft return on request, with no build work beyond writing the playbook and uploading the documents.
shortlist.tradeoff: Someone must start each return by hand, which does not scale to dozens of runs a day, and the routing, approval and audit trail would depend on the person's discipline.

approach.text: The steps are fixed and known in advance (sort, extract, assemble, check, approve), and the only judgement is reading the documents. A workflow with AI steps gives predictable, testable runs at lower cost than an agent, which would multiply token use. The rules' choice of workflow stands.

topology.text: Routing comes first because W-2s and 1099s need different extraction handling, and a cheap sorting step lets each type use simpler instructions. The evaluator add-on turns the checklist into an automatic reviewer that catches errors before a person sees the draft.

tools.text: I departed from the rules' main tool, which was the Claude app. Taxpayers upload documents into intake, so each return needs a trigger and fixed steps that run dozens of times a day, and that is n8n's job. Claude stays as the AI step inside the workflow. The supporting pieces are the same as the rules' set, with the Claude-only Skill replaced by a system prompt and resources that n8n can use.

hosting.text: Cloud, pay as you go, is the right fit for uncertain volume of 300 to 1,500 runs a month. Own hardware would sit idle and would need staff, which the firm does not have. Metadata-only tracing keeps tax data out of telemetry.

autonomy.text: Level 2, approve every output. Every draft is a sign-off point because it goes to a taxpayer, is hard to undo and involves personal data. Starting with a shadow stage on about 20 real returns earns trust before any widening, and the spouse-death pause stays with a trained employee.

models.text: Haiku sorts documents, as a cheap and fast router that is a cost lever. Sonnet does the extraction, the main judgement work. Opus is the checker, a different model from the worker, so the checker does not share the worker's blind spots. The rules left the checker unspecified, and this is the required separation for personal data. Starting capable and stepping down after tests matches the guidance.

shortlist.text: n8n is the main tool because the process is triggered by uploads, the steps are fixed, and the approval gates are visible. Claude is the alternative because it can run a draft on request, but it fails at this volume and leaves audit to the person.
